applicable_when: The kernel permutes NCHW->NHWC. Input is contiguous (stride-1 in x/HW), so loads are coalesced. Output stride is (150528,1,672,3): channel c is stride-1 in memory, but c is mapped to the YBLOCK (slow) axis. Consecutive threads in a warp differ in xindex (HW), producing store addresses 3 floats apart (stride-3). NCU confirms 23% excess sectors and only 20/32 bytes utilized per store sector. Fix: swap tile axis assignments so XBLOCK covers the N*C=30 dimension (making c the fast thread axis, stride-1 in output) and YBLOCK covers the HW=50176 dimension. Add @triton.autotune to explore tile sizes and recover the 54.9% occupancy gap.
